AssetCapacity1: The 6 MiB limit counts unique normalized bytes across private, archived and historical uploads. The 500 limit counts distinct version records, including versions sharing bytes. Source artwork is separate. Upload: 3 MiB maximum; processed image: 1 MiB maximum.
AssetCapacity2: Encoding and metadata are outside the 6 MiB allowance, but count toward the storage payload. No separate derivatives are generated; originals are not retained. At capacity, reuse an existing version or arrange a separate storage expansion. Archiving does not free retained bytes.
AssetCapacity3: GitHub requires a configured credential and a private repository, checked before upload. Public or unverified repositories are refused. The complete formatted storage payload also has a 16 MiB limit.
AssetPicker1: Upload or choose an exact image version. Save the field afterward; publishing is a separate step.
AssetPicker2: Archiving hides all versions from routine selection. Every saved reference remains available.
AssetUpload1: Still PNG, JPEG or WebP · up to 3 MiB, 4,096 pixels per side and 8 megapixels. Stored as a verified WebP up to 1 MiB. Titles and source notes stay private.
CardWorkshop1: Configure faction, type and printed slot before first publication. Once published, duplicate the card to change those fields while preserving existing deck references.
CardWorkshop2: Source card identity and printed values are read-only. Duplicate this card into an authored set to configure a new definition.
CardWorkshop3: After changing the effect, review the displayed wording and run an engine test.
CatalogControls1: Availability never grants player ownership. Archiving stops future acquisition; existing ownership and gameplay legality are retained.
CatalogControls2: Membership describes this set. Each card's legality and acquisition settings remain separate. Limited formats use the existing pack recipe and require complete rarity pools.
CatalogControls3: New recipes are not automatically sold. New products start unavailable with no prices.
CatalogControls4: A new permanent identity is assigned when you save. This creates shared draft content only.
CatalogControls5: This printing shares its gameplay definition. It requires explicit appearance ownership and is excluded from every acquisition pool.
CatalogControls6: Faction and card type follow the selected compatible effect. Its declared parameters can be edited in Mechanics. Artwork starts from its existing immutable image; change it in Artwork.
CompetitionWorkshop1: Configure future Ranked seasons and free Gauntlet events. Existing competitions retain their original rules. Published scoring, schedules and prizes are locked; duplicate to change them.
CompetitionWorkshop2: Pause prevents new matchmaking. Cancel permanently stops new play; completed matches and promised earned rewards remain. Archive retires entry while existing runs can finish within their original window. These changes take effect after publication.
CompetitionWorkshop3: Exact player presentation from the saved draft. Times are local; entry remains subject to runtime availability.
DeckCompositionField1: Blank dates leave the window open. A blank limit is unlimited. Refunded purchases count toward the lifetime limit.
DeckCompositionField2: Leave a currency blank to disable it. Zero is a free claim. No default price is assumed.
DeckCompositionField3: References use the same published release. Opponent assignments require qualified AI effects and no legacy boss additions.
DeckWorkshop1: Author a reusable composition for players, practice or a compatible encounter. Publishing a recipe grants no cards or cosmetics.
DeckWorkshop2: This legacy template describes the engine's standard deck or an encounter's existing additions. Duplicate it to create an independent authored composition; the original setup remains in its encounter.
DeckWorkshop3: Internal notes stay outside release packages and public APIs. GitHub storage requires a private repository.
EngineWorkshop1: Use Live or Saved draft, configure a custom starting state, then execute legal engine commands.
EngineWorkshop2: Assign this effect to a compatible card and save the draft before testing it.
EngineWorkshop3: Workshop rules are not available yet. Refresh Admin after the server update completes.
EngineWorkshop4: This rule is not available in the deployed registry. Choose a supported rule from the list.
EngineWorkshop5: The registry definition is read-only. Edit a card to select this effect or change its parameters.
EngineWorkshop6: Hand size applies to creation and refill. Payment, damage, targeting, priority, matchmaking, timers, progression and rewards remain engine-controlled.
MechanicsEditor1: Save this reference, then test the exact saved draft. A mechanic revision affects all referencing cards in future games.
MechanicsEditor2: Existing source handler; only declared parameters are editable. Switching to composition starts a new definition and does not translate this ability.
MechanicsEditor3: Build automatic abilities for the existing arming action. Effects resolve top to bottom, before the defender receives priority.
MechanicsEditor4: Select this controlled armament through the attack's weapon choice. Pay the normal attack cost; no new activation cost or response window is introduced. Conditions evaluate once from the accepted payment and pre-attack state. A failed condition still consumes the selected weapon. Each ability resolves once in order, with at most four abilities and four effects each.
MechanicsEditor5: Attack bonuses add to existing modifiers for this combat only. Life gain is immediate and does not expire. The source stays attached until combat ends, then goes to discard; it cannot be selected again while attached. There is no turn-based usage reset. Opponents use the existing block and priority windows after declaration. Other timings, targets, durations, recursive triggers and scripts are unsupported.
MechanicStudio1: Create reusable executable mechanics. The shared release pins their interpreter and definition into each game. Revising a mechanic changes its referencing cards in future games; existing games keep their captured behavior. V1 supports two-player games; Free-For-All rejects decks using these mechanics until its multiplayer interpreter is implemented.
MechanicStudio2: Support triggers require non-Servitors. Attack, block and payment triggers require Servitors. Placement uses the ordinary free end-placement or existing faction placement action.
MechanicStudio3: Activations are optional choices made with priority. Costs commit only after all source, target and payment checks pass.
MechanicStudio4: Attach this mechanic in a compatible card's Mechanics section. New definitions do not grant ownership or sell cards.
OfferWorkshop1: Publish a recipe, its exact printings, deck box, card back and explicit price together. No purchases or grants happen in this preview.
PrintingWorkshop1: Each printing uses this card's gameplay identity and mechanics. Edit gameplay in Details or Mechanics; the fields below affect only the selected printing.
PrintingWorkshop2: Printing membership is separate from gameplay-card membership and limited-format pools. Set assignment alone grants no acquisition or ownership.
ReleaseReview1: Local edits are not included. Save them or discard them before publishing.
ReleaseReview2: Open Design and save a field to begin a shared draft. Return here to validate, preview and publish it.
ReleaseReview3: An accepted engine action is a release check, not a guarantee of comprehensive balance testing.
ReleaseReview4: Review the saved release before restoring it. Historical releases are immutable.
ScenarioBuilder1: This configures a temporary test, not a played history. Unassigned value/suit slots remain in the deck. Deck entries are drawn first, in the order shown. Start a new test to apply changes.
EncounterWorkshop1: Starting life and scripted attacks. Attack progression offset changes the attack sequence; it does not reorder chapters.
EncounterWorkshop2: Select a supported ability and its parameters. Ability wording is presentation; the selected rule controls behavior.
EncounterWorkshop3: Each selected card adds one copy. Up to 12 different cards per side, from this encounter’s faction.
GauntletPlaytest1: Select a card to test this effect, or open the encounter that owns this mechanic.
